text: The organization is the boundary. Control Hub is the console where users, roles, locations, services, and devices are made real. Every later room assumes this map.
Control Hub is the single dashboard Cisco documents for managing users, permissions, calling, meetings, messaging, and devices. [cite:1]
The first sign-in can start a setup wizard; accepting terms creates the organization, and the activation email address is the sign-in identity used to set the administrator password. [cite:1]
People you add start with no administrative privileges. A full administrator assigns prebuilt roles, and can also assign roles to groups. [cite:2]
Locations organize users and workspaces by a physical address and are also where calling is anchored. [cite:3] [cite:4]

Symptom: New admin still sees a read-only UI Likely cause: Role change has not propagated, or the browser session is old Check: Role is saved on the user. Clock time since Save. Article allows up to 10 minutes. Fix: Wait, sign out, sign in again. Do not stack a second role “to force it.”

Symptom: Cannot assign location admin to an existing full admin Likely cause: Location administrator is exclusive Check: User already has another administrator role Fix: Remove the other roles first. Known issue: location admin cannot combine with other roles, including custom roles.

Symptom: Group role did not apply Likely cause: Directly assigned role conflicts with the group role Check: User has a direct read-only or location administrator assignment Fix: Remove the incompatible direct role, remove the user from the group, add them again.

Symptom: Inherited badge does not match the checkboxes Likely cause: Documented known issue with group-inherited roles Check: Compare group assignment to the user role page Fix: Trust the article’s known-issue note; do not invent a second bug. Re-check membership.

Symptom: Device admin cannot open Calling configuration Likely cause: Role limitation, not a broken service Check: User is device administrator or user and device administrator Fix: Use a full administrator, or a role the Calling docs allow. Do not “upgrade” the device admin in place without reading the matrix.

Symptom: Users cannot open a TAC case in the app Likely cause: Redirect user support is on Check: Organization Settings → Help and support. Admins are exempt per the article. Fix: Decide if that redirect is intentional. Turning it off restores the non-redirected path described in the article.

Symptom: Location has a caution and calling does not work Likely cause: No telephone number on the location Check: Calling article: a caution means you have not configured a telephone number; you can’t make or receive calls until you do. Fix: Add a number using the PSTN option for that location. PSTN choice is T2-R02.

Symptom: Cannot delete a location Likely cause: Users or workspaces still reference it Check: Services → Calling → Numbers, filter to the location Fix: Remove users and workspaces first. Numbers return to the PSTN provider. Delete can take up to an hour.

Symptom: Activation code does nothing Likely cause: Code typed into the wrong device, or device not yet on the network Check: Devices page still shows the device as waiting. Read the error on the device and on Control Hub → Devices. The string changes by device family, so regenerate the code from Control Hub rather than reusing a screenshot. Fix: Regenerate from Control Hub rather than reusing a code from a screenshot. Confirm the device family in a later room.

Symptom: CSV export of admins changed under you Likely cause: Filter was edited before the download finished Check: Article: wait until the CSV downloads before changing the filter Fix: Re-export. You cannot manage roles through that CSV.

Symptom: Webex site admin cannot see a site Likely cause: Site is still Site Administration managed, or the user has not signed in once since the role was assigned Check: Article: site admin roles apply to Control Hub-managed sites, and the user must sign in to Control Hub once after assignment Fix: Confirm site management mode. Have the user sign in once.
L0 What is Control Hub? Cisco’s management console for one Webex organization: users, permissions, calling, meetings, messaging, and devices. [cite:1]

L1 Why does it exist — what breaks without a single org console? Services, identities, and devices would be administered as separate products. The overview exists so an admin sees which services are actually provisioned before configuring them. [cite:1] [cite:5]

L1a What breaks if only one person holds full administrator? Cisco recommends more than one full administrator so the org stays operable. The partner’s administrator is the first full administrator and is expected to create more. [cite:2]

L2 How does an admin action work end to end? Sign in, change a user or location or device, and the org record is what later services read. Role grants can take up to 10 minutes. A device is not in the org until its activation code is used. [cite:2] [cite:1]

L2a Where do licenses sit relative to users? The Get Started article says the overview is where you view licenses across services and administer licenses to users. Organization-based and group-based license assignment are full-admin privileges in the role matrix. The SKU catalog is T1-R03. Read the strings on the subscription in Control Hub. They follow the order, and the role matrix only covers privileges. [cite:1] [cite:2]
L2b Are locations only a calling idea? No. The locations article says you can use one location for both calling and workspaces, and that settings templates can apply to groups and locations. [cite:3]

L3 What are the failure modes, and how do I prove which one? Prove it from the user role page, the group membership, the location caution icon, and the Devices state — not from the symptom sentence. The matrix in this room is the checklist.

L3a How do I prove a role conflict versus a delay? If Save was moments ago, the 10-minute window is still open. If the user already holds location admin or read-only, combination rules explain a refused or ignored grant. [cite:2]

L3b How do I prove Calling is “missing” because of role, not because the subscription lacks Calling? Check the overview for whether Calling is provisioned [cite:1] , then check whether the signed-in admin is a device administrator or user and device administrator, who can’t administer Webex Calling. [cite:2]

L4 How does this admin model differ across Calling, WxCC, WxCCE, and Dedicated Instance? Control Hub remains the org console. Webex Calling configuration is a service inside it, and device-centric admins are explicitly blocked from administering Calling. [cite:2] Contact Center adds a Contact Center Service Administrator role; a customer full administrator can administer contact-center features, while a customer read-only administrator cannot access the Webex Contact Center…

L4a What is different about external contact-center admins? A partner full administrator can perform contact-center admin similar to a customer full admin, except they cannot add or revoke Contact Center Service Administrator from other external administrators. A read-only admin from a partner org can access contact-center admin interfaces in read-only mode; a customer read-only admin cannot access them at all. [cite:2]

L5 If I redesigned Control Hub roles, what would I change, and what stops me? I would want one location-scoped role that can also hold a narrow custom permission. The product constraint that stops me is explicit: location administrator cannot be combined with other roles, including custom roles. The supported escape hatch is a custom role that includes the needed view, not a stack of badges. [cite:2] [cite:8]

L5a What would I not automate? Role assignment via the administrator CSV. The article says you can’t manage administrator roles through that CSV. [cite:2] Read developer.webex.com for which roles the API can assign. Coverage changes when Cisco adds a role, so check that page before any script is trusted.

Which combination does the role article forbid? B. Location administrator is exclusive, including versus custom roles. More than one full admin is recommended. [cite:2]

A user-and-device administrator says Webex Calling settings are missing. The overview shows Calling is provisioned. What do you check before you open a TAC case? The role itself. User and device administrators and device administrators can’t administer Webex Calling. [cite:2]

You assign a role to a Webex group, then remove Jordan from that group. What happens to the admin rights that came only from the group? Jordan loses those permissions. Group membership is the grant. [cite:2]

Confirm the permission exists in the UI. Security activity administrator is the prebuilt role tied to the admin actions audit log in…

A customer read-only administrator cannot open contact-center administration, but a partner read-only administrator can open it read-only. Is that a contradiction? No. The contact-center role table documents those two rows differently. [cite:2]

In one sentence: what is a workspace, and how is a device bound to the org? A workspace is a place (room, desk, lobby) that can hold devices and services. Control Hub issues an activation code that is entered on the device to link it. [cite:3] [cite:1]

Directory Connector is one Windows instance per Active Directory domain. SCIM 2.0 is a REST sync with no on-premises connector. Org SSO maps uid . Partner SSO maps mail . A dry run comes before the first full sync, and invite suppression requires SSO.
One Directory Connector instance serves one Active Directory domain. Download it from Control Hub. A trial or any paid subscription is required to reach the software. [cite:1]
The only required cloud attribute is uid . Cisco recommends mail or userPrincipalName , and the chosen attribute must be in email format. [cite:1]
Do a dry run before the first full synchronization. Incremental sync stays disabled until a full sync has completed. Group synchronization requires a full sync. [cite:1]
Organization SSO uses a SAML 2.0 NameID of transient and a uid claim. Partner SSO uses mail , rather than uid . [cite:2]

Commercial SCIM tenant URL is https://webexapis.com/identity/scim/OrgId/v2 . Webex for Government uses https://api-usgov.webex.com/identity/scim/OrgId/v2 . The manually retrieved bearer token is valid for 365 days. [cite:3]

Symptom: Control Hub still shows directory synchronization disabled Likely cause: A full synchronization has not succeeded. Check: Connector dashboard, Sync Now. Fix: Finish install, dry run, then full sync.

Symptom: Incremental sync is greyed out Likely cause: No completed full sync, or a sync is already running, or sync is paused. Check: The Start incremental sync conditions. Fix: Complete a full sync first.
Symptom: Groups never appear Likely cause: Only an incremental sync was run. Check: Synchronization mode. Fix: Run a full sync for groups.
Symptom: Users from a second domain are missing Likely cause: One connector instance cannot serve two domains. Check: Installed instances versus domains. Fix: Install one connector on each domain.
Symptom: Connector will not sign in Likely cause: The Windows login is not the full Control Hub admin. Check: Account comparison. Fix: Use that full admin account for connector sign-in.
Symptom: uid mapping warning Likely cause: The chosen attribute is not email format, or it is not mail or userPrincipalName. Check: The connector pop-up. Fix: Map mail or userPrincipalName.
Symptom: Invite suppression does nothing Likely cause: SSO is not integrated. The feature requires it. Check: SSO status. Fix: Finish SSO, then suppress invites.

Symptom: SCIM Test Connection fails for a less-privileged session Likely cause: The bearer token was minted by an account that cannot create users. Check: Who was signed in when the token URL ran. Fix: Use an incognito window and a full admin.

Symptom: Duplicate cloud users after Entra sync Likely cause: userPrincipalName does not match the Control Hub email, so Webex treats them as new. Check: Attribute map, userName. Fix: Map the Entra attribute that is the email address.

Symptom: Cleared Entra attribute still shows in Webex Likely cause: Entra ID does not synchronize null values. Check: The attribute is NULL in Entra and unchanged in Webex. Fix: The article points that limitation at Microsoft.

L0 What is the only required mapped field? uid. [cite:1]
L1 Why does a dry run exist? The guide says you must do a dry run before a full synchronization. [cite:1]
L1 What breaks if SSO is skipped and invites are suppressed? Invite suppression requires the SSO integration, so the suppression step is not available as a standalone switch. [cite:1]
L2 How does an organization SSO assertion name the user? The IdP claim includes the uid attribute, and NameID format is transient. [cite:2]
L2 How does partner SSO differ? The claim is mail, rather than uid. [cite:2]
L3 Which SCIM generation synchronizes groups and still skips rooms? SCIM 2.0. Rooms and avatars are Wizard-only, through Microsoft Graph. [cite:3]
L3 How long is the manual SCIM bearer token valid? 365 days. [cite:3]
L4 Why would SAML JIT create fail while Directory Connector is healthy? If Directory Sync or Entra ID is enabled, SAML JIT create or update will not work. [cite:4]
L4 What proves a second IdP is configured and still unused? Control Hub can add the IdP and leave it inactive until a routing rule exists. [cite:4]
L5 Where does the Calling routing prefix belong? In the location dialing settings, not already inside the Directory Connector extension. T2-R03 cites that rule. [cite:7]

L5 Can this identity move to another GEO later? The residency article says Webex does not currently support migrating between GEO locations. The country choice permanently sets the GEO for users and encryption keys. [cite:5]

Automatic assignments grant Calling, Meetings, Messaging, and Contact Center when a person is added. A license typed onto a new user at creation skips that template. Webex spends the oldest subscription first. Calling still needs a location and an extension or number. A professional workspace license does not downgrade to common area.
Organization and group templates combine. If one template adds a license and another removes the same license, the user still receives it. [cite:1]
Existing users is checked only for the save you are making. The next visit shows it unselected. Preserve licenses for existing users is selected for you when you choose Existing users. [cite:1]

Nested groups do not inherit the parent group’s license assignment. The groups hierarchy in Control Hub is flat. A user’s effective licenses are still the combination of every group assignment they belong to, including the parent, when those assignments are applied to them. [cite:1]
Webex Calling standard and Customer Assist cannot both be assigned to one user. Webex Attendant Console requires the Calling service set to Professional. [cite:2]

A workspace upgraded to the professional workspace license cannot be downgraded to a common area workspace license. A user downgrade from professional to standard loses provisioning and configuration for the affected users. [cite:3]

Templates, then the Calling exception: Automatic licensing grants Webex licenses to new users without a manual assignment for each person. The organization path is Management, Users, Licenses. Oral answers: 30 seconds. Automatic templates cover future users. I can also apply them to existing users for one save. Organization and group templates union. Subscriptions are consumed oldest first. Services are usable when the user is Active.

Symptom: Template licenses never land on a new API or CSV user Likely cause: A specific license was assigned at creation. Check: The create payload. Fix: Create without a specific license if the organization template should apply.

Symptom: Existing users did not change on the second visit Likely cause: Existing users does not stay selected between sessions. Check: The scope checkboxes after you reopen the page. Fix: Select Existing users again and Save.

Symptom: A removed license is still on the user Likely cause: Preserve licenses was left on, or the other template still grants it. Check: Both templates. Fix: Clear Preserve only when removal is intended. Remember the union rule.

Symptom: Nested group members missed the parent licenses Likely cause: A group assignment applies to direct members. Nested groups do not inherit. Check: Group membership depth. Fix: Assign the license on a group the user belongs to directly, or rely on the combination once both assignments apply.

Symptom: Attendee is missing for a site admin Likely cause: Attendee is unavailable for the Webex Site Administrator role. Check: Site administrator roles. Fix: Remove those site privileges, then assign Attendee.

Symptom: Preserve toggle stays off after Cancel Likely cause: Known issue: cancelling the warning does not restore the enabled state. Check: The toggle after Cancel. Fix: Re-open the assignment and set the toggle again. The article records the issue.
Symptom: Standard Calling and Customer Assist will not save together Likely cause: The individual-edit article forbids the pair. Check: The two checkboxes. Fix: Keep one of them.

Symptom: Calling settings error immediately after the license add Likely cause: The article’s recommended recovery is remove and reassign. Check: The error on Calling settings. Fix: Remove the Webex Calling license and assign it again.

Symptom: Professional workspace will not return to common area Likely cause: The upgrade article says downgrade is not available. Check: The workspace license. Fix: Plan the professional workspace as a one-way change.

Symptom: Calling VAR Professional is FALSE and a number is present Likely cause: The directory number is the wrong format, already assigned, or not on a provisioned location. Check: user.csv Phone Number column. Fix: Provide an unassigned E.164 number on a Calling location.
L0 What does an automatic license assignment do? It grants the selected Webex licenses to new users without a manual assignment for each person. [cite:1]
L0 When can the person use the service? When they become Active, at first sign-in, unless verified domains, SSO, and suppressed invites already made that possible. [cite:1]
L1 Why would a template ignore a brand-new user? A specific license was assigned at creation. API and CSV follow the same rule. [cite:1]
L1 Which subscription is used first? The oldest, until its licenses are used, then the next oldest. [cite:1]
L2 What is the union rule? Organization and group templates combine. A license added by one and removed by the other is still received. [cite:1]
L2 Do nested groups inherit? No. The assignment applies to direct members. The hierarchy is flat. [cite:1]
L3 What does Preserve licenses protect? Licenses already on existing users when you remove them from the assignment. Clear it to remove those licenses, including manually assigned ones. [cite:1]
L3 Which Contact Center license wins a group collision? The Premium agent license. [cite:1]
L4 Why can Calling stay off after the template is correct? The user needs a location and an extension or number. Auto-assign looks up an E.164 work number that is pre-provisioned and free. [cite:4]
L4 What does a professional workspace upgrade refuse afterward? A downgrade to the common area workspace license, including when you switch subscriptions. [cite:3]
L5 What is lost on a professional-to-standard user downgrade? All provisioning and configuration information for the affected users. The article says to treat that as a last resort. [cite:3]
L5 Which Calling client versions lose Calling services? Webex Calling versions 44.3 or earlier. [cite:3]

A location is a physical address that can hold both calling and workspaces. A user belongs to one location. A workspace belongs to one location. Webex generates a Location ID. Changing the location time zone does not change the time zone already stored on an auto attendant, hunt group, or call queue.
Create a location at Management > Locations > Manage location > Create manually. Name, country or region, and street address are required. Webex generates a Location ID. [cite:1]
A user can be assigned to only one location. A workspace can be assigned to only one location. Manual add from the location is up to 25 users. [cite:1]

A location with Webex Calling cannot be deleted until you click Disable calling. Calling users or workspaces on it cannot be removed from the location until the Webex Calling license is removed. [cite:1]

Puerto Rico, Guam, American Samoa, and the U.S. Virgin Islands need the territory as the country when you want territory-specific numbers. Setting the country to the United States blocks those numbers. [cite:1]
Calling locations that collided with a workspace location during migration were renamed with a -CALL suffix. Cisco does not support double-assigned workspaces. [cite:1]

The address is the anchor: Locations organize users and workspaces by a physical location identified by an address. The same location can carry calling and workspace management. The article’s header on the retrieved page is June 05, 2026. [cite:1]

Oral answers: 30 seconds. A location is a physical address. One user, one workspace. Webex issues the Location ID. Calling and workspaces can share it. I do not delete a Calling location until I disable calling and remove Calling licenses from the people and places that still have them.

Symptom: Delete location is refused Likely cause: Calling is still configured, or Calling users and workspaces remain. Check: Calling tab and the user list. Fix: Disable calling. Remove Calling licenses from the people and workspaces that still have them.

Symptom: CSV upload created a second copy Likely cause: Location ID was filled in on a row that was meant to be new, or edited on a row that should have stayed. Check: The Location ID column. Fix: Blank for new. Do not edit for existing.

Symptom: CSV delete removed nothing you intended, or removed extra rows Likely cause: The file must contain only locations to delete, and Location ID is required. Check: The CSV contents. Fix: Remove every location you want to keep, including its Location ID.

Symptom: Map never appears Likely cause: The street was not chosen from the suggestion list. Check: Whether a suggestion was selected. Fix: Pick a suggested address, then move the pin. An unrecognized address can still be saved.

Symptom: Territory numbers are refused Likely cause: Country is United States for Puerto Rico, Guam, American Samoa, or the U.S. Virgin Islands. Check: The country on the location. Fix: Set the country to the territory.

Symptom: Two locations named Location1 and Location1-CALL Likely cause: Migration renamed a colliding calling location. Check: The suffix. Fix: Optional consolidate: copy, delete Location1, rename Location1-CALL.
Symptom: Calling workspace will not move Likely cause: Calling license is still on it. Check: Workspace services. Fix: Remove Calling, move, re-entitle.

Symptom: User gained or lost licenses when added to a location Likely cause: The organization template applied, and preserve license was off. Check: Whether a group template, CSV, or API was the path. Those are excluded. Fix: Read the template before you use the location user tools.

Symptom: Schedule hours are wrong after a time-zone change Likely cause: AA, hunt group, and call queue do not follow a later location time-zone edit. Check: Feature create time. Fix: The article says the feature time zone cannot be altered after creation.

Symptom: Workspace missing when filtered by calling location Likely cause: A double-assigned workspace is filtered by the workspace location. Filtering by calling location hides it. Check: Workspace details versus Calling > Numbers search. Fix: Assign one location. Search the workspace name under Calling > Numbers to see the calling location.
